request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

agent.result_text:
All the sheets of a tree now share one number sequence, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests (the main "tree numbering" test and scenarios 1–3).

**What changed:** only `takeNextNumber` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/ClaimRepository.java`.
- When a claim gets a number, the app now finds the tree the sheet belongs to. It follows the `parent` setting up to the top sheet, then collects every sheet under that top sheet.
- The new number is one more than the highest number given on any sheet of that tree. It's saved as that sheet's own last number, so the existing `lastNumber(sheetId)` lookup still works as before.
- It locks the top sheet's row before taking a number, so two claims opened at once anywhere in the tree get different numbers in turn.

**What stays the same:**
- Numbers already given are left alone, and no database migration was needed.
- Per-period numbering (`P1-1`, `X-1`) still runs per sheet.
- Every path that hands out a sheet number uses this one method, so all of them now follow the tree: opening a claim, splitting, reassigning, transferring a person, and cloning a sheet.

**Limit:** if someone changes a sheet's parent at the same moment a claim is being numbered, the lock could cover the old tree rather than the new one. I didn't guard against that.
